name: Galerie Rudolfinum
records_note: Posts annual reports from 2012 to 2025 with revenue tables and partner logos, but no financial statements or board list.

name: Kunsthalle Praha
watch: Petr Pudil co-owned coal firm Mostecká uhelná from 2005 and sold Czech Coal in 2010. About 30 people protested at the February 2022 opening.
why_flagged: Founded and funded by the Pudil Family Foundation (Petr Pudil co-founded BPD Partners, property and agrochemicals); partners bdp nadace, MyClinic and Dentons. Czech state gave no money at opening.
records_note: It posts Czech annual reports for 2020 to 2025 with accounts and auditor's report, names its board and lists partners and donors.

name: Fondation Donwahi
funding: Founder Illa Donwahi's own funds (agribusiness), private patrons and annual partner grants.
records_note: The foundation has no working website: its domain is a for-sale page. No reports, accounts, funder list or board were found anywhere.

name: Picha / Lubumbashi Biennale
funding: Founders' own money, private donors and Belgian and French agencies. 2026 Biennale sponsors: Belgian foreign ministry, Wallonie-Bruxelles, Enabel, Africalia, Pullman, Africell, TMB bank.
watch: Artist-led; urgent funding call in August 2026.
records_note: Shows the 2026 Biennale sponsors as a page of logos and lists its curators and staff, but publishes no reports, accounts or board.

name: Centro de Arte Contemporáneo de Quito
funding: Run by the Fundación Museos de la Ciudad, a nonprofit acting on commission of the Quito municipality. Admission is free.
watch: Housed in the old military hospital, San Juan district. Part of the Sistema de Museos Quito. No controversy found.
records_note: The foundation running it posts yearly accountability reports from 2016 to 2025 with budgets and transparency files; it names no funders and no board.

name: Medrar for Contemporary Art
funding: Space set up with support from Young Arab Theatre Fund, Foundation for Arts Initiatives, Abbara, Roberto Cimetta Fund, Netherlands Embassy in Cairo and AFAC through a Swiss SDC grant.
watch: Artist collective since 2005; runs the Cairo Video Festival. AFAC lists a 2019 North Africa Cultural Program grant. No current budget is published.
records_note: Names its founding supporters in one undated About sentence and lists no board; it publishes no annual reports or accounts.

name: Kumu Art Museum
funding: Part of the state-funded Art Museum of Estonia.
records_note: A thank-you page names about 30 funders and partners without a year and the About page lists the supervisory board; no reports or accounts.

name: EMMA Espoo Museum of Modern Art
funding: City of Espoo, plus the Saastamoinen Foundation collection.
records_note: Posts activity reports for 2006 to 2024 with key financial figures, names its two main corporate partners and lists its board; no full statements.

name: Serlachius Museums
funding: Gösta Serlachius Fine Arts Foundation, endowed from a paper and forestry fortune.
records_note: The foundation page names its seven board members, but no annual report, accounts or donor list is posted on the museum site.

name: Frac des Pays de la Loire
funding: State through DRAC Pays de la Loire and Région Pays de la Loire. Main patron Fondation Sodebo since 2012; Collection RAJA backed the 2024 Veilhan show.
watch: Food and packaging patrons. No flagged funder, protest or censorship found.
records_note: Names its main patron Sodebo and a 2024 project patron on its patronage page, and names its president and staff; no reports, accounts or board.

name: 49 Nord 6 Est – Frac Lorraine
funding: French state (DRAC) and Région Grand Est; patron list unreadable.
records_note: Lists its board of directors in a 2025 booklet on its site; patron names are not published, and no annual reports or accounts are posted.

name: Le 19, Crac
funding: French state (DRAC Bourgogne-Franche-Comté), Région Bourgogne-Franche-Comté, City of Montbéliard and Pays de Montbéliard Agglomération.
watch: Public money only; no censorship or protest found.
records_note: Names its four public funders in its About text; publishes no annual reports, accounts, private sponsors or board list.
